on the verse "You shall dwell in sukkos
"And afterwards, 'they shall dwell in sukkos,' etc.
Rather, the first is for the guests,
the second for the people of the world, etc.
Fortunate is the portion of Yisrael,
דִּכְתִיב: כִּי חֵלֶק ה׳ עַמּוֹ וְגוֹמֵר
as it is written, 'For Hashem's portion is His people,' etc.
is the illumination of the seven holy middos
as is stated there in the holy Zohar:
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר.
'For in six days Hashem made,' etc."
And the souls of the seven shepherds
for his own middah in holiness, as is known.
the illumination of the seven holy middos
in all the souls of Yisrael.
For the aspect of the three holy Avos
is found in all the souls of Yisrael,
in that they are merciful, bashful, and doers of kindness.
is the middah of "kindness to Avraham,"
to do kindness with all creatures,
even with one who is not worthy;
and therefore dross came out of him.
"'So that His fear may be upon your faces'
And it is the aspect of contraction;
yet in this too there is dross.
the one in the middle, who joins the two middos,
to one who needs it and is worthy.
The aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
is that he is the teacher of all Yisrael
and imparted the Torah to them.
Regarding the aspect of Aharon HaKohen,
it was said at Matan Torah (Shemos 19:6):
"And you shall be a kingdom of kohanim";
for so it was set in the souls of Yisrael,
that they be servants performing the holy service,
"And you shall be called kohanim of Hashem."
By the aspect of Yosef HaTzaddik
And the aspect of Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
is the heart of all Yisrael,
"The heart in the body is like a king in a country."
And he is "the man raised on high,"
עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה, א),
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah (Avodah Zarah 5a),
and he is the aspect of Mashiach,
who is the individual who repents
for whose sake the whole world is forgiven;
that is, he will bring the way of teshuvah
into the hearts of the souls of Yisrael.
there is found such a soul
into the heart of the totality of the souls of Yisrael.
And the illumination of the seven holy middos —
it is within the power of all the souls of Yisrael
because they are all a G-dly portion from Above.
And on this the holy Zohar cites:
as it is written, 'For Hashem's portion is His people.'"
And through the holiness of the sukkah we merit
to have drawn into our souls
the illumination of the seven holy middos.
And to this alludes "You shall dwell in sukkos
seven days" — "the first is for the guests";
to have set firmly in our souls
Therefore the essence of the mitzvah of sukkah comes
שֶׁהֵמָּה עִיקַּר סִיבַּת הַחַיִּים שֶׁל הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
which are the main cause of the life of the soul,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה נִשְׁפָּע בָּנוּ
and through this there will be drawn into us
life from the illumination of holiness.
And regarding this the verse uses
"So that your generations will know," etc.,
and it does not use the wording "so that you will remember,"
as it says regarding Yetzias Mitzrayim
לְמַעַן תִּזְכּוֹר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ וְגוֹמֵר.
"So that you will remember the day of your going out," etc.
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּאֵינוֹ כְּדֵי לִזְכּוֹר לְבַד,
Perforce it is not merely in order to remember,
because what is brought about through the mitzvah of sukkah
that is, the recognition and feeling of the heart,
in the inwardness of the heart,
of the illumination of His holiness, blessed be He.
And to this the holy Zohar alludes:
that is, the illumination from Above
that is drawn into all the souls of Yisrael
through the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah.
alludes to the preparation for this
on the part of the soul,
which comes only by way of emunah,
as in the saying, "He is Truth,
that is, His illumination, blessed be He,
to shine the light of all seven
into the heart: the truth of His providence, blessed be He.
And the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
that is, all the souls of Yisrael together —
only from the aspect of emunah,
to receive the illumination from Above
Men of the Great Assembly instituted that we say
Certainly the season is set apart for this
just as Pesach is "the time of our freedom,"
since we went out of Mitzrayim,
and Shavuos is "the time of the giving of our Torah,"
that they learned this from the wording of Scripture:
for regarding Pesach the Torah mentions
no expression of rejoicing at all,
only "And you shall make a Pesach to Hashem your G-d"
whereas regarding the festival of Shavuos it says
(ibid. 11), "And you shall rejoice before Hashem your G-d."
For on Pesach, although they had
the illumination of His countenance, blessed be He,
nevertheless, because it was only for the moment
and was at once concealed from them,
when the process of Yetzias Mitzrayim was completed
"And you shall rejoice before Hashem your G-d";
that is, from this rejoicing is born in the heart,
since it brought us all the way before Him, blessed be He.
And as is known, in all the holy convocations
from then on for all generations,
when this time arrives each year.
וְהִנֵּה בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת נֶאֱמַר גַּם כֵּן
Now regarding the festival of Sukkos it also says
"And you shall rejoice before Hashem your G-d
seven days" — with the four species.
to come before Him, blessed be He,
וְעַל זֶה אָנוּ מְשַׂמְּחִים לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ
and for this we rejoice before Him, blessed be He,
as stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 30:2):
"Whoever takes the palm branches in his hand —
אָמְנָם עוֹד יֵשׁ נוֹסָף בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת
Yet there is more added regarding the festival of Sukkos:
the expression "And you shall rejoice in your festival"
that is, a special rejoicing from Hashem, blessed be He,
by virtue of the holiness of the festival,
through the surrounding light of the mitzvah of sukkah.
And for this a special name was given
that it is called "the time of our rejoicing."
(Pesikta DeRav Kahana, the supplementary piska for Sukkos)
counts three times that an expression of rejoicing
is mentioned in the holy Torah
including also "And you shall be only joyful"
לְרַבּוֹת יוֹם טוֹב אַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג
to include the last day of the festival
even the day of Shemini Atzeres —
from the root of the holiness of the festival of Sukkos,
that Shemini Atzeres is the absorption of
the holiness of the festival of Sukkos,
just as the festival of Shavuos is
the completion of the holiness of the festival of Matzos.
That is, from the joy of the holiness of Sukkos
the joy is set and absorbed
for all the days of the year.
And this is what is alluded to in the verse
that is, permanence and being are given
that is drawn down on this festival,
so that a small remnant remain
from which the impression will remain,
so that the joy be set in the heart
for all the days of the year.
It is stated in the Pesikta
(Pesikta DeRav Kahana, the supplementary piska for Sukkos):
For if they were liable to exile,
the Holy One, blessed be He, accounts it to them
as if they had been exiled to Bavel,
from the hand of your enemies.'"
like the difficulty raised by the Tur
"that I made Bnei Yisrael dwell in sukkos," etc.,
"when I took them out of the land of Mitzrayim"
the festival of Sukkos should have been held
And to this the wording of the Pesikta is directed:
But why does it bring this verse,
found regarding the exile of Bavel?
It may be said in this,
that in this verse it says
that specifically the cause of the exile
brings about the completeness of the redemption,
as it says, "There you shall be rescued;
from the hand of all your enemies" — specifically.
when all of Yisrael's sins have been forgiven.
And known is the saying of our Sages of blessed memory
כָּל שֶׁלֹּא נִבְנָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּיָמָיו
"Anyone in whose days the Beis HaMikdash was not built
is as if it was destroyed in his days."
And since we have not merited,
that the redemption come in our days,
it is evident from this that we have not yet merited
וְעַל זֶה אָנוּ עוֹשִׂין מִצְוַת סוּכָּה,
For this reason we perform the mitzvah of sukkah,
as we say in the Yehi Ratzon
"In the merit of my going out of my house to the outside,
may it be reckoned for me as if I had wandered far away."
For the mitzvah of sukkah is
and to take shelter in all one's affairs
in the shadow of His wings, relying on His providence, blessed be He;
the matter of the refinement of the exiles:
to take shelter in Him, blessed be He,
in all the subjugation and troubles,
to come to know that everything comes
from His guidance, blessed be He,
"And I will set My throne in Eilam," etc.
And although the mitzvah of sukkah
already existed in the time of the First Temple,
on the first Yom Kippur they saw
that the rectification was not complete
as it had been before the damage,
"I said, you are G-dly beings," etc.,
as we discussed on Shabbos Shuvah.
This is what is alluded to by
"And on the day that I make account, I will make account" (Shemos 32:34):
some of the damage is accounted for and reduced,
And for this the mitzvah of sukkah works
as it says, "There you shall be rescued" — specifically —
As we find that in the exile of Bavel
and Yechezkel saw the entire Work of the Chariot,
and all the secrets of the Chariot are set out there,
which permission was not given to expound,
And specifically in Bavel was established
"Ezra came up from Bavel and established it;
Rabbi Chiya and his sons — and they established it";
and two yeshivos never ceased from them,
And certainly the intent is not specifically
כִּי כְּמוֹ כֵן כָּל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת פּוֹעֲלִים
for likewise all the exiles bring about
the drawing near of the redemption
and the increase of new Torah insight
כְּאָמְרָם זַ״ל (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, ד, ח):
"Many tzaddikim did she raise up in her destruction,
more than in her settled state";
regarding Rabbi Zeira, who would avoid
Rav Yehudah, because he wished to go up to Eretz Yisrael;
"Whoever goes up from Bavel to Eretz Yisrael
'They shall be brought to Bavel, and there they shall remain
until the day that I remember them.'"
אִם הוּא מְדוּיָּק רַק עַל גָּלוּת בָּבֶל
if it refers strictly only to the exile of Bavel
that came after the First Destruction,
surely the time of remembrance was already completed
and from then on the mitzvah to go up applied again;
עַל שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ חוֹמָה (יוֹמָא ט, ב).
for not going up like a wall (Yoma 9b).
after the destruction of the Second Temple.
is a name borrowed for all the exiles,
because it was the first of the exiles;
and so in this exile as well
the command is, "There they shall remain
until the day that I remember."
And likewise in every kind of exile
the drawing near of the redemption is brought about
inwardly in all the souls of Yisrael,
as it says, "There you shall be rescued,
and there Hashem will redeem you from the hand of your enemies,"
It is stated in the holy Zohar
"Whoever is of the stock and root of Yisrael
sits under the shade of faith."
that Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
was the first of the converts (Chagigah 3a),
כְּאָמְרָם זַ״ל (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, טז, א):
And nevertheless he is called a native,
That is because it was made clear afterward,
until Hashem, blessed be He, testified about him
that the root of his birth was in holiness,
"Yours is the dew of your youth" —
the Holy One, blessed be He, said:
And this is the matter mentioned in the Midrash
'And the dwelling of Bnei Yisrael,' etc."
And certainly the intent is not
that the calculation of the years
rather, it refers to this matter,
that the root of one's birth is in holiness;
not from the side of a person's comprehension
but from the side of connection to the root
And this is what is mentioned in the holy Zohar
above the aspect of the Name Havayah,
that is, from the aspect of Atika;
and there is the aspect of his connection
Therefore the Shabbos meal of Atika Kadisha
הוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
as is known from the holy Zohar
this is the meal of Atika Kadisha."
וְהִנֵּה עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית כא, ח):
on the day Yitzchak was weaned";
and it is stated in Tosafos
(שַׁבָּת קל, א, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל שָׂשׂ אָנֹכִי):
that is, on the day Yitzchak was circumcised at eight days.
For he was the first soul
to be circumcised at eight days,
meaning that his root was in holiness
and from him holiness descended to his offspring,
that they be "borne from the womb";
and they are called "Your people are all tzaddikim,"
because "from the womb they are circumcised for Your Name";
that is, holiness is rooted in them
"For through Yitzchak shall offspring be called yours";
And for this Avraham then made
a great feast "on the day of hi-gamel,"
for then it became clear to him
that about him too Hashem, blessed be He, testified
that the root of his birth too is in holiness,
since he begot such holy offspring,
from whom the holy seed would descend for generations,
who would be bound by their birth
And to this the Midrash alludes
"The Great One of the worlds was there";
that is, the root shone forth
which is the aspect of Arich Anpin;
And from this the joy in his heart grew,
since there was made known to him
and so he had no need to fear
And along these lines we heard
in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory,
that if he knew for certain about himself
that he is of the seed of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov —
that is, that in the root of his birth
he is bound up with holiness —
he would walk with his hat
כַּנָּהוּג מִי שֶׁהוּא שָׂשׂ וְשָׂמֵחַ בְּעַצְמוֹ
as is the way of one who is glad and joyful in himself
because he goes his way securely
from our holy Rebbe, of blessed memory,
שֶׁעִם כָּל זֶה יוּכַל לִפְעוֹל זֹאת
that even so, one can bring this about
that he be considered as being, from the root of his birth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
is as we find with Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
whom they wanted to disqualify from the congregation
עַל פִּי דִּין וּסְבָרָא שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה,
according to the law and reasoning of the Torah,
and only through mercy did he bring it about
on the basis of received tradition:
"a Moabite man, but not a Moabite woman."
And it is like what we said
regarding Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
that his meriting to be called Yisrael
as is stated in the holy Zohar
"Your fathers dwelt beyond the River of old":
"For from a distant place He brought him near,
כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר: וָאֶקַּח אֶת אֲבִיכֶם;
as it says, 'And I took your father'";
that is, through an arousal from Above,
from the aspect of Heaven's mercy.
And let us return to the matter:
to this the holy Zohar alludes:
"Whoever is of the stock and root of Yisrael" —
that is, one who is confident about himself
that the root of his birth is in holiness —
he "sits in the shade of faith"
and take shelter in Him, blessed be He, with his emunah
because he has a connection to the root;
וְלָכֵן אֵין לוֹ לִפְחוֹד מִשּׁוּם רָע,
and therefore he has no need to fear any evil,
Now the people of Yisrael as a whole
that is, they are bound by their birth to the root,
in the inwardness of the point of their heart,
"It is revealed and known before You
that our will is to do Your will;
only the leaven in the dough holds us back."
וְזֶה נִתְגַּלָּה עַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת סוּכָּה,
And this is revealed through the mitzvah of sukkah,
so that through it we have
and from this joy is drawn to us
which is "the time of our rejoicing,"
עַל פָּסוּק: וַיַּעַשׂ אַבְרָהָם מִשְׁתֶּה גָּדוֹל:
on the verse "And Avraham made a great feast."
